title: Inefficiency in CSG Module
body:
### Tested versions

- 4.4.1 / master

### Issue description

In `csg.h`, the function `_regen_face_aabbs()` is used to build an AABB for every `Face`.
It gets called by `CSGBrush::copy_from()`, `CSGBrush::build_from_faces()` and `_unpack_manifold()`.

As far as I can tell, these are never used. Instead `CSGShape3D::_get_brush()` implements something similar, which is used for the `CSGShape3D`'s `get_aabb()`.

Considering this AABB is calculated and kept in memory for every face out of potentially hundred thousands, I feel this should be addressed.

Additionally, Manifold provides a `BoundingBox()` function. It might be faster just to run that on the output manifold.

---

Another can of worms: Manifold (especially with TBB) is quite fast. It offers a bunch of other great functionality that would benefit Godot users (LevelSet, Hull generation, (De-)Compose, ...).

I feel like using manifold merely as a new backend for the pre-existing CSG system does not leverage it's potential.

I'm currently working on a PoC terrain generation system similar to [Deep Rock Galactic's](https://youtu.be/Vtmac_f4Pzs?si=Kv6fqGU6ukJcS2IF&t=195) using parallelized manifold operations in a GDExtension to acheive persistent real-time deformations.

Maybe one day we can stop saying 'The CSG nodes in Godot are mainly intended for prototyping.'

I'd love to turn the results of my experiments into engine contributions. If anyone with experience is interested in helping me out by answering some questions from time to time, please reach out ❤️
